content.label: It’s perfect, I mean perfect, it’s a really nice UI and easy to use and it connects perfectly with Apple Health. It just works and looks amazing while doing it.
Great gentle encouragement to start and continue your exercise routine

title.label: I love my Gentler Streak App

content.label:
I love the app! It tells me how good I have done after a work out and lets me know I should take it easy if I’m not feeling great but can still push through if I’m feeling good to go! 

It’s all very helpful. I also like seeing maximum heart rate reached and also my exercise zones and how hard I worked in my work out.

With the new ability to rename workouts gentler streak is even better than ever. Apple should consider buying it and replacing their activity tracker as it is far superior. When iOS 18 is released with the ability to change the colour of icons it’ll be a total winner in every way.

I really like the motivational notifications that come after a workout has been completed, and enjoy the visual glance of how I am tracking. The paid version has some additional capabilities but for day to day the free app seems to suffice for me. Highly recommended.

Even though I’ve read the explanation for the reason I keep getting the ‘overreaching’ notifications (gaps in exercising etc), I’ll be cancelling my subscription and deleting the app… Even after reading the explanation for the incorrect feedback, it’s really off-putting as I’m only doing light walks and light yoga, which I’m pretty sure even on a daily basis, should be okay for most people’s fitness levels. However, if there are any updates or fixes that may correct this in the near future, I would still be keen to know about these as other than this, it’s a great app.

I like the concept but it is pulling stats wrong from the Garmin connect app. For example, average running cadence, the Garmin connect app has one number, this app pulls through a completely different number from the connect app so something isn’t right with it. Also does the same with maximum heart rate stats for workouts.

title.label: Not yet worth the subscription costs

content.label: As someone who overtrains, struggles to take rest days and honestly gets too invested in “closing the rings” I had high hopes for this app. However the visualizations are limited, you only see a short time period and the insights were not particularly useful or meaningful. The suggested workouts were things like 2hour runs at the moderate level (I typically run 60-90min 6-7 days per week with one 2.5hr run) and taking the slider to the right suggested an insane 19 hour walk. Over time this may develop into a great app but it’s not there yet.

title.label: Great alternative to built in goals

content.label:
This app takes a different approach to encouraging fitness which is way more realistic than the built in monthly goals the Apple Watch gives you out of the box.

I’ve been finding my monthly challenges getting more and more intense, where the outcome seems to be getting you to just do more than last month every month. This is not sustainable and after getting the monthly challenge for the last 2 years, I’ve ended up with an activity goal that is simply out of reach.

Gentler Streak takes a different view and lets you look at your fitness over more than a single day, which is way more reflective of real life. If you work out heaps for a few days it tells you to rest. If you take a few rest days it encourages you back again. If you get sick or want to take a longer break it can account for that.

I’m pretty much converted off the Apple challenges now, and just work to keep my streak in a healthy range.

It’s well worth the subscription, and I’m glad I tried it. The developer is also super responsive and helpful answering questions.
